sb_prompt: WHY DO YOU THINK THAT ONLY ABOUT HALF OF ELIGIBLE VOTERS IN AMERICA TAKE PART IN NATIONAL ELECTIONS
turns: That's weird, I mean it seems like half the country just doesn't care at all, but my cousin says he's voting for the first time this year after hearing so much about how hard it is to get a handout without one.
Yeah, actually that part does make sense to me, but honestly I've made my choice years ago and can't really say why.

Yeah, but I guess it's weird because I work at a front desk all day and see people begging for gas money or rent, and honestly, that makes me feel like the whole system is broken rather than just needing a vote to fix it.
I get that feeling when you see people right there in front of you, but I still think the bigger picture matters even if you can't see the fix immediately.
I guess that's the thing though, because if the system is actually broken like I think, then how does one vote even fix that?
I mean, it doesn't fix everything overnight, but it's the only way to make sure someone is actually listening to the people who need help, even if the fix takes a while to show up.
Yeah, but if they aren't even listening to the people needing help, then who exactly are we voting for?
Look, it's not about picking a perfect person who instantly solves everything, it's just about having someone there to answer the door when things start to go sideways.
That's a fair point, I guess, but it still feels like watching someone hold a door open while the whole building is on fire, and you're just waving them in.
I mean, you know, maybe the building isn't on fire just yet, maybe it's just got a leaky roof and we're voting to get the repairs paid for before the water gets everywhere.
You're right, I guess I'm just used to seeing the building burn down around me every day.

I mean, maybe I'm just old school, but I've seen enough people rely on that leaky roof staying dry for a long time that I don't want to risk letting it out in the rain just because the building looks bad from the outside.
I mean, that leaky roof story makes some sense, but honestly I've seen a few of those "repairs" turn into a whole new fire instead of a fix.
I guess that's just what happens when you leave it in the hands of folks who think they know better than the people living in the building, huh?
Yeah, exactly, because then the only people who know what the fire is doing are the ones selling us the fire extinguishers.
Yeah, but I'd say that's part of why people don't vote, not why they should stop.
Yeah, but here's the thing, I feel like most of those people aren't even given the brochure in the first place, let alone asked to fill it out.
Oh, that's the other half of it, isn't it? They're just not even handed the map to begin with.
Yeah, that's exactly it—like if I don't even have the map, how the heck am I supposed to find the door?
Yeah, that's probably the real deal-breaker for a lot of folks, because if the door isn't even on the map, nobody's gonna knock on it unless you're standing right in front of it already.
Yeah, that's the thing, it feels like they're just waiting for you to show up so they can tell you where the door is.
Yeah, that's the scary part, isn't it? You don't know if you're even allowed to look for the door until you've been standing in the rain long enough to get sick.
Yeah, it is just exhausting waiting for permission to even start looking.
Yeah, I know what you mean about the waiting, but honestly that rain thing is just part of the price of admission for actually getting to knock on the door yourself.
Yeah, maybe I'm just too used to waiting for the door to magically appear rather than walking out to find it myself.

Yeah, I get that feeling of just waiting for something to happen to you, but that's exactly why showing up changes the game—you stop being the person waiting in the rain and start being the person holding the umbrella.
Yeah, I suppose the umbrella thing is kind of hopeful, but looking at the receipts I get every week, I'm starting to think I'm the one who just needs to learn how to make my own shelter.
Yeah, but I'm still not gonna let you stand out there in the storm just because you think you have to build your own shelter.
Yeah, but I'm starting to feel like if I just stop waiting for the umbrella to appear, maybe I'll get burned out before I ever even find the door myself.
I mean, building the shelter yourself is one thing, but trying to open that door in the storm without even knowing which way the wind is blowing? That's just asking to get drenched.
Yeah, maybe that's why I just don't want to get drenched trying to find a door that might not even exist.
You know, maybe the door doesn't exist at all, maybe it's just a story they tell you to make you feel small enough to take the handout without asking for the key.
Yeah, maybe you're right, but honestly it just feels like if I knock on a door that's supposed to be locked, I'm gonna get told to take off my boots anyway.
Yeah, but I'm saying that once you finally get the door unlocked, that's when you start seeing what's actually inside the room.
Yeah, but if I take off my boots, the floor is gonna soak right through to my socks, so I'm not even sure I want to go inside yet.
Look, I know the floor feels wet right now, but if we don't step inside to check where the holes are, we're just standing there getting soaked forever.
Yeah, but if I get my socks wet, then I'm just standing in a puddle waiting for someone else to come dry me off anyway.
Yeah, but if you stay out there in the puddle, you're never gonna dry off no matter who shows up.
Yeah, but if I never step in there to check, I'll just keep standing there forever, so maybe I'll finally take off those boots and see what's actually on the floor.
Yeah, but maybe that's the only way to see what the floor actually looks like without just standing in the cold wondering if it's wet or not.
